newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies McVeigh request for new trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies McVeigh request for new trial.

text.p: The judge in the Oklahoma City bombing case on Monday denied Timothy McVeigh's request for a new trial and said he would impose a formal sentence on the the Gulf War veteran on Thursday.
McVeigh was convicted and sentenced to death by a jury in June for the April 19, 1995 bombing of the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City that killed 168 people.

In a written order, U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch said: "All of the questions and issues raised in the defendant's motion have been considered and ruled on in the course of pre-trial proceedings and during the trial, and the court adheres to those rulings."
The judge's 2-1/2-page order said nothing in the defendant's request justified calling a hearing.
McVeigh was found guilty of the bombing on June 2 and the same jury on June 13 sentenced him to die. He is being held in a suburban Denver federal prison.
Requests for new trials are often filed, but seldom granted. The judge's order said that McVeigh is to appear on Thursday morning for his formal sentencing.
McVeigh's alleged co-conspirator Terry Nichols is scheduled to go on trial Sept. 29.

McVeigh asked for a new trial based on 13 grounds including an alleged juror's remark during the trial, immense pre-trial publicity and emotional testimony by survivors and relatives of people who died in the bombing.
